title: Spuriousness-Aware Meta-Learning for Learning Robust Classifiers

problem.claim: Image classifiers can rely on spurious input-target associations, causing poor generalization when those associations change.

gap.claim: Existing mitigation commonly assumes annotations identifying spurious correlations, which is impractical in many settings.

contributions.claim: SPUME is a meta-learning framework that iteratively detects and mitigates spurious correlations without requiring them to be known beforehand.
The framework uses a pre-trained vision-language model to extract image attributes, curate varied class-attribute correlations, and measure their spuriousness.
Its meta-learning tasks use support and query sets with different highly spurious correlations to encourage classifier invariance.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly present SPUME and its spuriousness metric as novel contributions.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report robustness to spurious correlations without prior knowledge of those correlations.
The authors report the best performance on five benchmark datasets under different robustness measures.
The authors report that implementation code is available.

narrative_sequence.summary: Spurious correlations can mislead image classifiers and harm generalization under distribution changes.
Robustness methods are needed, but annotation requirements create a practical limitation.
SPUME iteratively identifies and reduces excessive reliance on spurious correlations.
Extracted attributes support spuriousness measurement and meta-learning tasks with deliberately differing correlations.
The resulting classifier is intended to become invariant, with reported robustness and benchmark performance.

source_observation.claim: Training tasks expose the classifier to support and query sets whose spurious correlations differ substantially.

interpretation.claim: Changing nuisance relationships across task splits may encourage reliance on more stable predictive signals.

application.claim: For robustness work, construct training episodes that vary suspected nuisance-target associations when such variation is available.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this strategy transfers to domains, attributes, or distribution shifts beyond those evaluated.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the five benchmark datasets or the robustness measures.
The abstract does not report numerical results, baselines, or ablations.
The abstract does not detail the spuriousness metric or meta-learning algorithm.
The abstract does not establish independent verification or reproducibility.
